claims.text: Enhanced short-range order in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles increases local bond strength.
Enhanced short-range order in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles increases cohesive energy.
The increased bond strength and cohesive energy caused by SRO delay premelting relative to a fully disordered state.
Rapid quenching produces chemically disordered CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Post-synthesis annealing near 500 °C for varying durations can induce varying degrees of SRO in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Advanced diffraction or spectroscopy can quantitatively determine the degree of SRO in these nanoparticles.
The quantified degree of chemical SRO mediates the relationship between local bonding and thermal stability.
Increasing SRO creates a more uniform and stronger bonding network.
Increasing SRO reduces the density of weak bonds.
Weak bonds facilitate premelting at nanoparticle surfaces.
Nanoparticles with greater induced SRO will have a higher surface-premelting onset temperature than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Nanoparticles with greater induced SRO will exhibit less premelting at a given temperature than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Rapidly quenched, chemically disordered nanoparticles have a lower premelting onset and more pronounced surface premelting.
The proposed SRO effect should hold from ambient temperature to near the nanoparticle melting temperature.
Comparable particle size and the absence of significant surface segregation or substrate effects are required for the proposed comparison.
Surface segregation, finite-size effects, and substrate effects may independently influence premelting.
DSC can record the onset temperature for appearance of a premelted surface layer.
In situ TEM can measure the extent and growth rate of the premelted surface region.
